item.title: FASTA stores sequence; FASTQ stores sequence plus per-base quality
item.content: FASTA represents sequence records with a `>` definition line followed by sequence. FASTQ records additionally encode per-base quality scores and therefore contain four logical lines per record in the common layout.
item.explanationMarkdown:
FASTA is appropriate when sequence itself is the essential information, for example many reference sequences.

A typical FASTA record:

```text
>seq1 description
ACGTACGT
```

FASTQ commonly represents sequencing reads together with base-call quality:

```text
@read1
ACGT
+
IIII
```

The quality string must correspond position-by-position to the sequence. For raw sequencing reads, loss of quality information can prevent many downstream quality-control decisions.

cards.prompt: What is the key information difference between FASTA and FASTQ, and why does it matter for raw sequencing reads?
cards.answerGuidance: FASTA stores sequence records without per-base quality; FASTQ stores sequence plus per-base quality scores. Quality scores are important for assessing base-call reliability and downstream QC of raw reads.
